headline: All majors above their 200-day lines with RSI overbought, but whales are moving coins to cold storage while stablecoins sit flat.
paragraphs: The regime is solidly long. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB are all trading above their 200-day simple moving averages, though none of them have printed a golden cross yet. That means the 50-day line has not crossed above the 200-day line on any major asset. The picture is an uptrend in place but not yet confirmed as a regime shift. Bitcoin at 72,757.66 is 41.7% below its 12-month high of 124,739.81; Ethereum at 2,344.26 sits 51.3% below 4,817.76. The market capitalization stood at 2.49 trillion dollars on the day, up 4.09% in 24 hours, with Bitcoin dominance at 58.4%. That concentration is stable and typical of a broad bid.

Momentum tells a different story than trend. Bitcoin's RSI-14 is at 80.2, Ethereum at 84.8, Solana at 77.7, XRP at 80.7, and BNB at 76.3. These are overbought readings across the board. MACD is above the signal line on every major except ADA, which shows MACD below signal. What we have is an uptrend that is running hard into overbought territory while confirming its direction on the momentum indicator. The tension here is between confirmation (all MACD above signal) and exhaustion (RSI above 75 on five of seven assets). When an uptrend is this extended on the momentum meter, it is still valid, but it is also fragile. The 24-hour move for BTC was 5%, for ETH 4.11%, and for XRP 20.65%. Over the last 7 days, XRP climbed 31.85% and ETH rose 25.27%. That acceleration is real, but the question is whether it persists when RSI rests.

Leverage positioning shows expensive longs with short-side liquidation bias. Bitcoin funding on OKX runs at 0.005% per 8 hours, annualized to 5.5%, which is moderate. Ethereum is higher at 0.01% per 8 hours, or 11% annualized. The long-to-short ratio on BTC is 1.07, meaning slightly more money is long than short. On Ethereum it is 1.18. On Solana it is 1.85, on XRP 1.42, and on Doge it is 3.6. These ratios signal heavy long bias, especially in Doge and Solana. Over the last 24 hours, liquidations favored the short side: Bitcoin saw 6.4 million dollars in long liquidations and 10.4 million in short liquidations. Ethereum saw 2.4 million in longs and 7.6 million in shorts. The pattern holds across all five majors tracked. Shorts are being flushed, which tells you the momentum run has real convictions behind it, but it also means there is less short protection if a reversal came.

Whale flows reveal a tension between institutional action and crowd sentiment. Over the past 24 hours, 250 million dollars moved off exchanges, net. Bitcoin accounted for 182 million of that outflow, Ethereum for 67 million. The two biggest moves off exchanges were 100 million in USDC from Coinbase Institutional and 69 million in BTC from Coinbase. The two biggest moves onto exchanges were 200 million in USDT to Binance and 115 million in USDT to Bitfinex. Over the last four weeks, the weekly trend shows off-exchange moves of 1.44 billion, 875 million, and 100 million dollars, with one week of 880 million moving back onto exchanges. The net is clearly toward cold storage, while stablecoins sit at 307 billion dollars, down only 0.22% in 30 days. That is a supply of dry powder that is not shrinking. Institutional money is taking coins off the bid and sitting on them; retail stablecoin float is flat.

ETF flows show consistent inflow. On August 19th, Bitcoin ETFs took in 517.2 million dollars and Ethereum ETFs took in 186.8 million. Over the last five sessions, Bitcoin recorded 816.7 million in net inflows and Ethereum 295 million. Same direction for three consecutive days on both. The cumulative Bitcoin ETF inflow is now 52.8 billion dollars and Ethereum 11.7 billion. This is traditional finance capital parking itself in spot instruments while derivatives are crowded and funding is elevated. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 62, labeled Greed, and has ranged from 25 to 62 over the last 30 days. That is a single swing from fear to greed with no mean reversion yet.

What to watch: a break below the 200-day line on any major asset, which would signal regime deterioration. A funding flip to negative on Ethereum or any altcoin, which would signal long-position exhaustion. A reversal in the daily whale outflows from off-exchange to on-exchange, which would signal accumulation fatigue. An RSI close below 70 on Bitcoin or Ethereum after a rest day, which would suggest the momentum charge is pausing. For now, the tape shows uptrend, overbought momentum, crowded longs, and institutional cold storage alongside flat stablecoin reserves. That combination can persist, but it requires continued buying to sustain the RSI levels. The pressure is on the bulls to prove the move is not just momentum retracement.
